title: When Actions Train AI: Emerging Responsibilities for Decision-Makers
affiliations: University of Milan and University of Milan

detail.title: When Actions Train AI: Emerging Responsibilities for Decision-Makers
detail.abstract: In this paper, we formulate a second-order moral principle, called 'Model Consistency Principle', designed to guide the moral reasoning of organisational decision-makers whose actions may contribute to the training of artificial intelligence (AI) models. Unlike conventional approaches in AI ethics that primarily address developers, regulators, or users of AI systems, this inquiry has focused on those moral agents who, while not directly involved in developing these technologies, nonetheless shape the rules that AI systems learn through their institutional or corporate decisions. The core claim of this principle is that when actions are liable to become part of an AI training set, a moral agent cannot simply act according to their own principles and criteria. Instead, they should also consider what rules an AI model might infer from their behaviour, ensuring that these inferences align with the criteria they would otherwise have followed. A decision that takes this principle into account, while aimed at reducing the weight of variables considered irrelevant in the rules inferred by the AI, will nonetheless need to consider these very variables precisely to avoid spurious correlations. Actions that would otherwise be morally permissible may cease to be so when considered within the context of AI training, not because they violate the agent's principles, but because they fail to adequately guide the AI model toward inferring the correct decision rule.

title: Sleep Deprivation and Academic Success in the Digital Era: A Study among College Students in Delhi
affiliations: Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies-Technical Campus and Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies-Technical Campus

detail.title: Sleep Deprivation and Academic Success in the Digital Era: A Study among College Students in Delhi
detail.abstract: Sleep deprivation has emerged as a significant concern among college students, with potential implications for their academic performance. Adequate sleep is crucial for cognitive functioning, memory consolidation, attention, and critical thinking, all of which are essential for success in higher education. However, the demands and challenges of college life often lead students to experience sleep deprivation. This research aims to explore the impact of sleep deprivation on the academic performance of college students and investigate the underlying factors contributing to this phenomenon. By understanding the effects of sleep deprivation on academic outcomes and identifying the causes, appropriate interventions and strategies can be developed to mitigate its negative consequences.

title: Adam Smith’s Doctrine of Natural Liberty- Bharat-UK FTA
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Adam Smith’s Doctrine of Natural Liberty- Bharat-UK FTA
detail.abstract: Adam Smithʼs An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776) represents a civilizational inflection point in the development of global economic thought. His doctrine of "natural liberty," often simplified in mainstream discourse, does not advocate the absolute abolition of tariffs nor a laissez-faire vacuum devoid of state intervention. Rather, Smith outlines a moral-philosophical and economic framework in which minimal but rational regulation enables human enterprise, curbs rent-seeking, and prevents protectionist capture by powerful commercial interests. This article revisits Smithʼs nuanced position to demonstrate how his insights on market expansion, specialization, and productivity enhancement laid the intellectual foundation for the modern theory of competitive advantage and the global trade architecture. By tracing the continuity between Smithian political economy and contemporary debates on trade liberalization, the analysis argues that Smith remains indispensable for understanding the tensions between protectionism, national interest, and global economic interdependence.

title: Revisiting the Failure of the Phillips Curve after COVID-19: A 2025 Update
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Revisiting the Failure of the Phillips Curve after COVID-19: A 2025 Update
detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has reignited fundamental debates about the stability, slope, and empirical relevance of the Phillips Curve. While the relationship between inflation and economic slack deteriorated during the pandemic, recent scholarship offers new insights that complicate simplified narratives about the curve's failure. This meta-analysis synthesizes evidence from pre-COVID panel studies and the rapidly growing body of post-2020 research. Earlier crosscountry analyses illustrate that the inflation-unemployment relationship is highly conditional on macroeconomic tranquillity, institutional structure, and inflation expectations, particularly during recessionary periods. Post-COVID research advances this perspective by uncovering substantial nonlinearities, structural breaks, frequency-dependent dynamics, anchored expectation effects, trend inflation interactions, and regional heterogeneity. The pandemic shock provides an empirical environment in which many conventional mechanisms behave atypically, yet recent studies show that the Phillips relationship re-emerges once expectations stabilize and supply disruptions ease. Integrating evidence from hybrid NKPC models, timevarying instrumental variable techniques, Bayesian structural break approaches, spatial panels, sectoral analyses, and explainable machine learning, this study concludes that the Phillips Curve has neither collapsed nor returned unchanged. Instead, its apparent instability reflects the interaction between forward-looking expectations, inflation persistence, structural labor-market transformations, capacity constraints, and global supply linkages. These findings reaffirm the importance of hybrid modeling frameworks and caution against interpreting reduced-form flattening as evidence of structural irrelevance.

title: Event-Contrastive Embeddings for Disclosure-Driven Equity Signals: A Theoretical Framework for Robust, Real-Time Signal Generation

detail.title: Event-Contrastive Embeddings for Disclosure-Driven Equity Signals: A Theoretical Framework for Robust, Real-Time Signal Generation
detail.abstract: This paper introduces an event-contrastive embedding framework for forecasting short-horizon stock returns from corporate disclosures and structured fundamental updates. Traditional financial text models rely either on dictionary-based sentiment or on generic language representations that are not optimised for capital-market events. We propose a task-specific contrastive objective in which each disclosure is encoded relative to a set of comparable filings, yielding representations that capture cross-sectional distinctions most relevant for price discovery. The methodology combines three components: (i) an event-standardisation stage that aligns filings by economic purpose; (ii) a contrastive encoder that embeds each event relative to a local reference set; and (iii) a directional calibration step based on meta-labelling. We evaluate the framework using information-coefficient (IC) statistics, block-bootstrap inference, and superior predictive ability (SPA) tests to guard against data-snooping. The architecture is intentionally model-minimal and computationally efficient, making it suitable for both academic replication and production deployment in quantitative research environments. While empirical validation is left to future work, the theoretical analysis and stylised illustrations demonstrate how eventcontrastive embeddings can systematise textual information and provide incremental insight beyond standard financial NLP baselines.

title: A Unified Framework for Decision Theory
affiliations: University of Edinburgh - Usher Institute

detail.title: A Unified Framework for Decision Theory
detail.abstract: This paper develops unified geometric and functional-analytic proofs of representation theorems in Expected Utility, Subjective Expected Utility, Cumulative Utility, and Cumulative Prospect Theory. The approach naturally handles infinite outcome/state spaces and non-simple measures. It generalises readily to accommodate dropping of the completeness axiom, and non-transitivity due to fuzziness. It differs from classical treatments such as those of Savage and Anscombe-Aumann, by taking the domain of preferences to consist of linear maps between vector spaces of signed measures. It is also possible to take the domain of preferences to be linear maps between spaces of utility functions, which does not require a randomisation device. The proofs are relatively compact because they make use of well-established mathematical results including the theory of Radon measures, the Hahn-Banach theorem and the theory of projective tensor products. The treatment here suggests that if boundedness of utility functions is abandoned, then any finite utility assignment to the St Petersburg, Pasadena and related games is consistent with the axioms of expected utility theory.

title: Functional Isomorphism in Complex Adaptive Systems: From Biological Physiology to Civilisational Breakdown
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: Functional Isomorphism in Complex Adaptive Systems: From Biological Physiology to Civilisational Breakdown
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether biological organisms and human civilisations share a common functional architecture. Using results from general systems theory, cybernetics, complexity science, and systems biology, it derives the universal functional problem-set that any multi-unit adaptive system must solve: resource transformation, distribution, coordination, defence, repair, cohesion, and growth regulation. These constraints define a narrow solution-space of viable architectures. The analysis shows that the subsystem structures observed in organisms and civilisations constitute functional homologies rather than analogical parallels. From this architectural equivalence follows a finite and theoretically deducible pathology space. Applying the systems-biology principle that failure is the inversion of function, the paper derives seven universal failure modes-metabolic, circulatory, defensive, signalling, organ-level, cohesion, and malignant-and demonstrates that documented forms of civilisational dysfunction map onto this set. Malignancy is used as a structural test case: its ordered sequence of regulatory escape, proliferation, boundary invasion, and defensive overload emerges directly from multi-level regulatory architecture. The paper derives the prediction that civilisational malignancy must follow the same ordering. The framework is falsifiable: deviations from the architecture-implied pathology structure invalidate the theory. By establishing functional isomorphism, the paper provides an integrative analytic basis for assessing systemic fragility and long-horizon governance risks in socio-ecological systems.

title: Data Analysis in Research Papers and Theses: A Comprehensive Guide to Using SPSS and Python for Statistical Analysis and Visualization

detail.title: Data Analysis in Research Papers and Theses: A Comprehensive Guide to Using SPSS and Python for Statistical Analysis and Visualization
detail.abstract: Effective data analysis is the cornerstone of rigorous research in academic papers and theses. This paper provides a comprehensive guide on integrating data analysis methodologies using both SPSS and Python to enhance research quality. Through a practical case study examining the relationship between student study hours, prior academic performance, and examination outcomes, this paper demonstrates step-by-step statistical procedures, visualization techniques, and data interpretation strategies. The analysis includes descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, ANOVA testing, and data visualization using both tools. This guide addresses the strengths and limitations of SPSS and Python, offering researchers practical guidance on tool selection, data preparation, analysis execution, and results presentation. The findings demonstrate that study hours significantly correlate with final examination scores (r = 0.833, p < 0.001), highlighting the importance of rigorous statistical analysis in educational research. This paper serves as a practical resource for graduate students, researchers, and academics seeking to enhance their data analysis capabilities for producing publication-ready research.

title: A Conceptual Model and Supporting Approach for EU Taxonomy Alignment with Green BPM
affiliations: , Technische Universität München (TUM) - School of Computation, Information and Technology, Technische Universität München (TUM) - School of Computation, Information and Technology and Technische Universität München (TUM) - School of Computation, Information and Technology

detail.title: A Conceptual Model and Supporting Approach for EU Taxonomy Alignment with Green BPM

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no competing interests relevant to this article to report.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) – Grant no. 465904964

detail.abstract: Increasingly, companies are obliged and incentivized through regulations to consider the impact of their business processes on the environment, in order to promote sustainable business practices. In particular, the EU Taxonomy for Sustainable Activities outlines criteria for when business practices contribute towards a sustainable future. However, it is unclear in how far existing methods for analysing and improving business practices, in particular those of the disciplines of Business Process Management (BPM) and Green BPM (i.e., a BPM variant focussing on environmental sustainability) can make use of those criteria and their underlying concepts. Therefore, we propose a conceptual model that combines concepts of the EU taxonomy and Green BPM, and clarifies the relationship of the two domains. This conceptual model is intended to provide clarity to Green BPM researchers and practitioners, and EU taxonomy experts, in order to bridge the gap between the two domains and to operationalize the EU taxonomy with Green BPM approaches. To guide the EU taxonomy's operationalization for various Green BPM approaches, we also develop an approach to support the conceptual model's application. We evaluate the semantics and pragmatics of our conceptual model. We find the aligned conceptual model to be semantically feasibly valid and complete; via an illustrative example and a focus group evaluation with Green BPM and EU taxonomy experts we also find that both it and the supporting approach provide utility to their intended audiences.

title: Economic Agency and Policy
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Economic Agency and Policy
detail.abstract: The concept of "Monetary Sovereignty" explains how some countries do not face financial constraints, but leaves open the question of what real resource constraints these countries face. Expanding on previous work by Fadhel Kaboub, Ndongo Samba Sylla and Scott Ferguson on the implications of MMT on the developing world, this paper introduces a parallel concept, called "Economic Agency" that offers the following answer: Countries' real resource constraints are reflected by the amount and composition of liabilities owed by holders and potential holders of the currency, both domestic and foreign. Specifically, Economic Agency considers the government's ability to enforce taxes, the domestic capacity to produce basic necessities such as food and energy, the cost of credit denominated in the domestic currency compared to credit denominated in foreign currency, and the domestic country's ability to manufacture complex products that are demanded by foreigners. The paper contrasts Economic Agency with other approaches that conceive of an international monetary hierarchy that is defined primarily by a country's access to liquidity facilities offered by the Federal Reserve by examining what nonfinancial needs are met by such facilities and what domestic solutions to those needs would imply. Finally, the paper briefly explains what a long term policy regime focusing on enhancing Economic Agency would require, entail, and need to overcome.

title: Inflation and the Two Sides of Banks: How Disinflation Replaces Liquidity with Lending
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management and Insper Institute of Education and Research

detail.title: Inflation and the Two Sides of Banks: How Disinflation Replaces Liquidity with Lending
detail.abstract: We study how inflation differentially affects banks' two lines of business, liquidity management and loan making. After a large disinflation episode without fiscal adjustment or banking reforms, banks' deposit-side revenue decreased, interbank lending shrunk, and banks made more loans, as we show with high-frequency bank data. Deposit collection and liquidity management were highly rewarded during high inflation, and net interest margin decreased by two-thirds after the stabilization. Using a difference-indifferences (DiD) design, we show that banks more productive in loan making grew, and those more reliant on liquidity management shrunk or closed. Banks pricing became more responsive to the benchmark rate. Industries more dependent on external funding grew more after disinflation, which suggests that stable prices helps growth via the lending channel that can be otherwise crowded out by liquidity management. Large heterogeneity in banks' lending and deposit rates during high inflation suggests that the differential financial sophistication is a mechanism of monetary non-neutrality.

title: Competition and Privacy in Off-Market Trading
affiliations: University of British Columbia (UBC) - Sauder School of Business, Northwestern University - Kellogg School of Management and Imperial College Business School

detail.title: Competition and Privacy in Off-Market Trading
detail.abstract: In U.S. equity markets, brokers route retail orders to wholesalers who execute them offexchange at prices beating the NBBO. We propose a new theory for why wholesalers offer these discounts: by executing retail flow, a wholesaler privately learns, implying information rents from subsequent on-exchange market making. These rents motivate improved retail pricing, potentially generating midpoint-or-better executions, a commonly observed pattern that classic adverse-selection or inventory models struggle to explain. Policy implications include: (1) enhanced trade reporting erodes information rents and can worsen retail prices; (2) order-by-order auctions, despite increasing competition, may also worsen prices by eroding information rents; (3) a request-for-stream mechanism increases competition while preserving information rents, improving retail pricing.

title: A Critical Appraisal of the Role of Digital Technologies in the Detection and Elimination of Modern Slavery and Labour Harm in Value Chains
affiliations: Edith Cowan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and

detail.title: A Critical Appraisal of the Role of Digital Technologies in the Detection and Elimination of Modern Slavery and Labour Harm in Value Chains

declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethics approval was required for this paper

detail.abstract: A growing body of research focuses on the role that digital technologies can play in detecting, recording and preventing labour harms and modern slavery in global value chains. Labour harm in global value chains takes many forms, including forced labour, bonded labour, child labour, wage theft, and occupational, health and safety hazards. We use the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights as a framework to assess the adoption of a range of digital technologies, undertaking a critical review of literature examining the application of digital technology to address labour harm and exploitation in value chains. A total of 31 papers were examined from a wide range of journals and conference proceedings. The applications examined include social media, digital apps, remote sensing, blockchain and modelling. The review reveals that while technologies are being deployed to further detection, they are rarely developed for the purpose of mitigation and remediation. It is likely this area will flourish as a sub-discipline but to progress it must develop a research agenda. We recommend that future research broadens the range of methods used to study the application of digital technologies, arrives at shared terminology, and develops stronger links with the information systems literature and discipline. We also recommend that the literature inquire into whether and how such tools are being used for mitigation and integration with business systems, not just detection of labour harms.

title: Measuring the Effects of Monetary Policy Surprises on Financial Market Volatility using a Component GARCH Model
affiliations: Western Michigan University

detail.title: Measuring the Effects of Monetary Policy Surprises on Financial Market Volatility using a Component GARCH Model
detail.abstract: Monetary policy announcements exert a direct and substantial impact on the levels of uncertainty and fluctuations experienced within financial markets. This research focuses on the volatility of financial markets, which is one of the channels through which monetary policy affects risk-taking. Monetary policy surprises are decomposed into target and path surprises, to capture the information effects of the Federal Reserve (Gürkaynak et al. (2005)). The finding shows that monetary policy surprises have a significant impact on the long-term aspects of financial market volatility, specifically in the stock and bond markets. The effect of the target surprise on the long-term components of financial market volatility remains significant, regardless of whether it is estimated together with the path surprise or with other factors. Furthermore, path surprises have an increasingly pronounced influence on the long-term component of treasury yield volatility as the term to maturity increases.

title: Reasoning in Debt Valuation *
affiliations: Arizona State University (ASU), W.P. Carey School of Business, Finance Department, Students

detail.title: Reasoning in Debt Valuation *
detail.abstract: Using sell-side debt reports on corporate bonds, I examine the underlying reasoning behind financial professionals' debt valuations. By prompting large language models on 13,879 reports, I identify recommendation-related topics, their associated entities, valuation channels, and sentiment. The main findings indicate that (i) debt analysts' topic attention is primarily focused on balance sheet and income statement items. (ii) The attention exhibits time-varying patterns, with increasing attention to cash and declining attention to profitability during the global financial crisis. (iii) The reasoning analysts employ systematically differs across credit rating categories: discussions of investment-grade issuers emphasize credit ratings, whereas those of high-yield issuers focus on financial fundamentals. (iv) Lastly, quantifying the texts from reports into a vector space using an embedding model, I show that analysts' information can explain bond returns beyond traditional bond-related predictors.

title: AI and the Early-Career Penalty: Evidence from Korea

detail.title: AI and the Early-Career Penalty: Evidence from Korea
detail.abstract: This paper examines how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) reshape labor markets using large-scale survey data from the Republic of Korea. I exploit the fact that the deep-learning breakthrough of 2012 was largely unanticipated and construct a shift-share instrument that combines 2012 industry employment shares with post-2012, industry-specific measures of AI diffusion. At the regional level, greater AI exposure between 2013 and 2022 leaves aggregate employment and wages essentially unchanged. Beneath this stability, however, the effects are highly heterogeneous. AI-based automation reallocates employment toward ICT occupations but generates sizable employment losses among new labor market entrants, consistent with an experience-biased technological change. Using data for the diffusion of generative AI models over 2022-2024, I find similar reallocation toward ICT employment, except that the adverse effects on young workers are even more pronounced. The evidence points to high adjustment costs in labor and higher education markets, amplified by the changing task content of technology, as the key mechanisms behind these distributional impacts.

title: The Value of Accessing the Stock Lending Market: Stock Lending Income Bond and Asset Prices
affiliations: Arkansas State University, Arkansas State University and University of Manitoba

detail.title: The Value of Accessing the Stock Lending Market: Stock Lending Income Bond and Asset Prices
detail.abstract: Long-term equity investors who lend shares to short-sellers can earn stock lending income in the form of short-selling fees. This study treats stock lending income as an additional source of return-similar to dividends-for stock lenders. We model stock lending income as a bond with a time-varying coupon, valuing stock lending income (SLI) using a Vasicek-like bond pricing framework. The SLI bond price and the expected return are related to the current short-selling fee. We suggest that when evaluating after-fee anomaly performance, one should adjust the returns of long-leg portfolios based on the short-selling fee. Numerical results indicate that this SLI bond can be valued at approximately 1% of the investment base. In other words, access to the stock lending market adds about 1% in value to an equity position-equivalent to roughly $239 billion in the U.S. mutual fund industry in 2023. We suggest that, because the market size of the mutual fund industry can be significantly undervalued, the regulatory agency should propose new reporting requirements for funds that heavily invest in stocks with high short-selling costs.

title: Unconventional Monetary Policy, Bank Liability, and Asset: Identification through Heteroskedasticity Innovations
affiliations: Western Michigan University

detail.title: Unconventional Monetary Policy, Bank Liability, and Asset: Identification through Heteroskedasticity Innovations
detail.abstract: This paper examines the effect of unconventional monetary policy, such as quantitative easing and forward guidance, on the bank balance sheets. The study uses market-based measures of monetary policy stance to examine the impact of unconventional monetary policies on both the liability and the asset side of banks balance sheets. Unlike previous research that concentrated solely on the asset side of banks balance sheets, the study examines how different liability components respond to unexpected monetary policy changes. The findings show that unconventional monetary policy significantly affects bank liability ratios. For example, the Fed funds rate shock exerts pronounced and lasting effects on the loan-to-deposit ratio, aligning with theories that emphasize medium-term adjustments in lending behavior. Additionally, our analysis reveals the resilience of the cash-to-deposit ratio against large asset purchase and forward guidance shocks. However, forward guidance does exhibit a notable impact on the loan-to-deposit and non-core liability ratios.

title: Tax Litigation Risk, Earnings Management and Corporate Governance: Evidence from Brazilian Listed Firms
affiliations: University of Coimbra Institute for Legal Research, Vila Velha University and Federal University of Espirito Santo

detail.title: Tax Litigation Risk, Earnings Management and Corporate Governance: Evidence from Brazilian Listed Firms
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between earnings management and tax litigation risk in Brazilian companies listed on B3, considering the moderating role of corporate governance and the temporal direction of the effects. We test the hypothesis that discretionary accounting practices increase corporate tax litigation, and that high-quality governance mitigates this risk. The sample comprises 254 non-financial firms observed from 2009 to 2024. We employ panel regressions (OLS, fixed and random effects), dynamic panel estimators (difference and system GMM), panel Granger causality tests, and simultaneous equation models (2SLS and 3SLS), complemented by quantile regressions and sectoral controls. The results show that earnings management is positively associated with tax litigation and Granger-causes future tax disputes, while no evidence of reverse causality is found. Listing on B3's Novo Mercado segment weakens the impact of earnings management on tax litigation, highlighting the moderating role of corporate governance. Sectoral heterogeneity is also observed, with stronger effects in high-risk industries. Overall, the findings indicate that tax litigation is a salient dimension of corporate tax risk shaped by accounting behavior and governance quality, suggesting that integrating tax risk into Enterprise Risk Management frameworks and strengthening governance mechanisms can reduce opportunistic practices and litigation in the Brazilian context.

title: Taming the Growth Machine: The Long-Run Consequences of Federal Urban Planning Assistance
affiliations: UC Davis and New York University

detail.title: Taming the Growth Machine: The Long-Run Consequences of Federal Urban Planning Assistance
detail.abstract: We study how the federal Urban Planning Assistance Program, which subsidized growing communities in the 1960s to hire urban planners to draft land-use plans, affected housing supply. Using newly digitized records merged with panel data across municipalities on housing and zoning outcomes, we exploit eligibility thresholds and capacity to approve funds across state agencies to identify effects. Planning assistance caused municipalities to build 20% fewer housing units per decade over the 50 years that followed. Regulatory innovation steered construction in assisted areas away from apartments and toward larger single-family homes. Textual evidence related to zoning and development politics further shows that, since the 1980s, assisted communities have disincentivized housing supply by passing on development costs to developers. These findings suggest that federal intervention in planning helped institutionalize practices that complicate community growth, with subsequent consequences for national housing affordability.

title: Monetary Policy Wealth Effects: Evidence from the 2015 Swiss Franc Shock
affiliations: Swiss National Bank - Study Center Gerzensee, FHNW School of Business - Institute for Finance, University of St. Gallen and University of St. Gallen - Swiss Institute of Banking and Finance

detail.title: Monetary Policy Wealth Effects: Evidence from the 2015 Swiss Franc Shock

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no conflict of interest to report.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the transmission of monetary policy to household consumption through wealth effects in a small open economy. As a natural experiment, we exploit the 2015 Swiss franc shock, triggered by the Swiss National Bank's unexpected removal of the euro exchange rate floor. Using granular administrative data from a retail bank, we document substantial consumption responses by households with portfolio exposures to the policy shock. We show that a 1% valuation loss on financial assets is associated with a 0.7% reduction in total spending in the quarter following the shock. This effect is driven by large-ticket spending rather than out-of-pocket spending, attenuates rapidly over time, and depends strongly on the magnitude of the valuation loss. Our results provide direct evidence of a sizeable, immediate, and short-lived wealth channel of monetary policy. They underscore the role of exchange-rate-induced asset revaluations in shaping consumption dynamics in open economies.

title: Remote and Hybrid Work and Productivity
affiliations: San Juan College, San Juan College and San Juan College

detail.title: Remote and Hybrid Work and Productivity
detail.abstract: This paper examines how remote and hybrid work have affected worker productivity and the performance of the United States economy. Data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, Federal Reserve Economic Data, International Monetary Fund, and Statista were used to compare economic conditions before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The findings show that flexible work helped many industries continue production during the shutdown and supported the recovery that followed. Although inflation temporarily lowered purchasing power, overall output and productivity improved as remote and hybrid work became more common.

title: The Nonprofit War on Workers. Weapons of Labor Violence: An Analysis of the Chinese-American Planning Council's Legal Tactics to Exploit Workers

detail.title: The Nonprofit War on Workers. Weapons of Labor Violence: An Analysis of the Chinese-American Planning Council's Legal Tactics to Exploit Workers

declarations.ethicsApproval: Home care workers volunteered to speak to the author about their experiences. Their consent for the author to publish their testimony was given in oral and written format to the Office of New York State Assemblymember Ron Kim, where the author served as legislative director from 2019-2024.

detail.abstract: With the increasing tendency of federal jurisprudence to undermine statutory labor protections, employees in precarious, low-skilled jobs face mounting challenges in safeguarding their rights in the workplace. In particular, the proliferation of mandatory arbitration clauses and the federal preemption of state labor laws have deprived workers in New York City's home care industry of meaningful avenues to address violations of labor law by their employers. These violations include wage theft and unpaid overtime work, sometimes spanning up to twenty-four consecutive hours. This report examines two such cases—Lai Yee Chan et al. v. Chinese-American Planning Council and Mei Kum Chu v. Chinese-American Planning Council—and seeks to elucidate the challenges workers encounter in defending their labor rights.

title: Machine Learning for Secure and Intelligent Information and Communication Technologies: A Comprehensive Review
affiliations: Cosendai Adventist University and Cosendai Adventist University

detail.title: Machine Learning for Secure and Intelligent Information and Communication Technologies: A Comprehensive Review
detail.abstract: The exponential growth of information and communication technologies necessitates advanced security architectures integrating machine learning as a cornerstone of modern ICT protection. This review systematically analyzes machine learning applications in securing communication systems, synthesizing 600+ peer-reviewed publications from 2018-2025. The review establishes a taxonomical framework organizing ML-ICT security applications across four dimensions: network intrusion detection, intelligent authentication mechanisms, privacy-preserving distributed learning, and adaptive network management. Deep learning approaches achieve 95% accuracy in zero-day attack identification, though adversarial robustness remains limited with current defenses effective against 70% of sophisticated evasion techniques. Emerging paradigms include quantum machine learning for cryptographic applications, neuromorphic computing achieving 1000× energy efficiency improvements, and federated learning architectures enabling privacy-preserving collaboration. Critical gaps include absence of standardized evaluation metrics, limited interpretability hindering regulatory compliance, and scalability constraints preventing deployment in environments processing beyond 100 Gbps. This synthesis provides researchers with an evidence-based foundation for developing next-generation secure communication systems capable of adapting to evolving threat landscapes while maintaining performance, privacy, and regulatory compliance requirements.

title: Epistemological Clergies: When Orthodoxy Blocks Rational Debate

detail.title: Epistemological Clergies: When Orthodoxy Blocks Rational Debate

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare. This research was conducted independently without institutional affiliation or external funding. The author practices law in Argentina but has no financial interests in the jurisdictions or doctrines analyzed. AI systems (Claude, Perplexity, Genspark) were used as computational assistants for dataset construction, statistical analysis, and literature search, as disclosed in the manuscript's methodological transparency note. All conceptual frameworks, legal interpretations, theoretical arguments, and substantive conclusions remain entirely the author's own work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involves analysis of publicly available legal scholarship, judicial decisions, legislative records, and aggregated labor/crime statistics from government databases. No human subjects research requiring ethics board approval. No individual-level data collected. All data sources are documentary and publicly accessible.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded independent research. No external grants, institutional support, or commercial funding.

detail.abstract:
Why is rational debate about criminal or labor law reform impossible in certain jurisdictions? 
This article proposes that dominant legal doctrines function as secular religions with memetic architectures immune to rational debate. 
Applying Daniel Dennett's framework on religion as natural phenomenon, I argue that extreme criminal guarantism, orthodox abolitionism, and unconditional defense of labor ultraactivity exhibit religious structures: (1) sacralization of concepts, (2) conversion of empirical disagreements into moral transgressions, (3) exclusion through costly signaling, and (4) ideological purity blocking gradualism. 
Quantitative analysis of 150 observations (50 jurisdictions × 3 legal domains) reveals strong negative correlation between clerical orthodoxy and reform effectiveness (r =-0.78, p < 0.0001). Argentina (CSI=0.89) achieves 0% reform success versus Chile (CSI=0.23) with 63% success. Uruguay eliminated labor ultraactivity achieving superior worker outcomes. Extreme cases: Venezuela (CSI=0.835, REI=0.125) versus New Zealand (CSI=0.305, REI=0.615).
Structurally, "epistemological clergies" (journals, chairs, associations) exhibit endogamic citation rates (87.3%) doubling hard sciences (34-42%), filtering epistemic competition through gatekeeping that privileges doctrinal purity over empirical effectiveness.
I propose Pragmatic Harm-Reduction Framework measuring success by verifiable harm reduction rather than doctrinal purity. Debate impossibility is not accidental but adaptive mechanism protecting memeplexes from competition. Complete dataset and replication materials publicly available at GitHub repository: https://github.com/adrianlerer/Extended-Phenotype-Institutionalism-contribution

title: Green Finance, Inflation, And Anti-Money Laundering: International Evidence
affiliations: Ton Duc Thang University

detail.title: Green Finance, Inflation, And Anti-Money Laundering: International Evidence
detail.abstract: We examine how green-finance development and inflation jointly shape AML effectiveness across 76 countries. Green finance lowers money-laundering risk through transparency and verification mechanisms, with stronger effects where regulatory frameworks are robust. Inflation erodes AML effectiveness and can overturn the risk-reducing impact of green finance at mean inflation levels. A renewable energy proxy shows weaker explanatory power, underscoring the importance of comprehensive green-finance measures. These findings extend Routine Activity Theory and the economics of crime by showing that the efficacy of financial innovations is contingent on macroeconomic stability. Policymakers should pair green-finance promotion with inflation control and supervisory capacity-building to secure durable AML gains.

title: Firm-Specific Information and Momentum
affiliations: Monash University

detail.title: Firm-Specific Information and Momentum
detail.abstract: This paper studies the relation between the instantaneous aspect of price inefficiency about firm-specific information (IPIFI) and momentum. Controlling for the interaction between IPIFI and past returns, past returns no longer predict future returns. Results are robust to controlling for IVOLs, transaction costs, illiquidity, and their interactions, and other explanations for momentum. Results also hold for the other ninety countries. High-IPIFI firms are firms with greater uncertainties related to their fundamentals. These firms are larger growth firms with higher information uncertainty, profitability variability, and opaqueness but lower limits of arbitrage. The results suggest that momentum is more likely to be a conditional effect rather than a main effect.

title: Creative Destruction with Common Ownership
affiliations: CEPR, University of Oxford - Finance and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Creative Destruction with Common Ownership
detail.abstract: We study how common ownership affects economic growth through creative destruction. We add a common ownership layer on top of the model described in Aghion and Howitt (1992) and then derive new equilibrium conditions. Common ownership increases innovative activities if innovations considerably improve productivity, while the effect is opposite if the improvements are relatively modest.

title: Enhancing U.S. Small Business Lending Through Predictive AI Credit Scoring: A Framework for Reducing Default Risk and Strengthening Economic Stability

detail.title: Enhancing U.S. Small Business Lending Through Predictive AI Credit Scoring: A Framework for Reducing Default Risk and Strengthening Economic Stability
detail.abstract:
Accurately assessing credit risk for small businesses has long been a challenge for financial institutions. Traditional credit scoring methods, which rely primarily on historical financial statements and limited credit history, often fail to capture the dynamic and multifaceted nature of small business operations. These limitations increase default probabilities, constrain access to financing for high-potential entrepreneurs, and reduce the efficiency of capital allocation.

This paper introduces a predictive AI credit scoring framework designed to enhance small business lending in the United States. The framework employs advanced machine learning techniques—including gradient boosting, ensemble modelling, and anomaly detection—in combination with alternative and multidimensional data sources, such as cash-flow patterns, transactional behavior, digital footprints, industry-specific risk indicators, and macroeconomic trends. By integrating these diverse inputs, the model provides robust, real-time, and multidimensional assessments of borrower risk, improves early detection of financial distress, and reduces misclassification errors compared to conventional scoring systems.

Empirical evaluation demonstrates that the predictive AI framework improves portfolio stability, lowers default probabilities, and expands access to credit for previously underserved businesses. The study further highlights the broader economic and policy implications for the United States: improved credit accuracy facilitates financial inclusion, supports entrepreneurial growth, strengthens systemic stability, and promotes more efficient capital allocation across the small business sector.

The findings indicate that predictive AI credit scoring serves as a strategic tool for the U.S. economy, enabling financial institutions, fintech platforms, and policymakers to make more informed, timely, and equitable lending decisions, thereby fostering a resilient and inclusive small business ecosystem while contributing to long-term economic growth.

title: Bridging Climate Finance and Debt Sustainability in Global Vulnerable Countries (GVC)
affiliations: VERITAS UNIVERSITY ABUJA

detail.title: Bridging Climate Finance and Debt Sustainability in Global Vulnerable Countries (GVC)
detail.abstract: After decade of aspiring to fulfill sustainability ambitions, we are still facing a polycrisis of complex and intertwined global economic, social and environmental challenges. Specifically, climate – related challenges (stemming from both acute and chronic risks) are responsible for a series of macroeconomic shocks which (by inducing economic disruptions and fiscal pressures) directly affect a country’s fiscal space and debt sustainability. Consequently, Global Vulnerable Countries (GVCs) will have to face higher borrowing needs and costs which can result in heightened refinancing risks and fiscal space reduction. Regrettably, this will result in fewer resources being available to fund adaptation and mitigation policies to reduce potential climate vulnerabilities. In fact, this also increases the probability of default of the GVCs and can feed into the climate Crisis – Sovereign Debt Doom Cycle. Therefore, this paper argued that Debt for – Climate – Swaps (DFCS) could unlock direct funding for climate – related spending to break the negative cycle. Fundamentally, DFCS can free up fiscal space beyond the direct savings generated by the debt swap by enhancing governments’ repayment capacity is well as lowering borrowing costs often linked to debt distress situation. However, policy action at both global and national levels is needed to foster a more favorable external environment as well as enhancing macroeconomic stability with reduced structural constraints to accelerate long term growth and development of those vulnerable countries. In other words, for these actions, global coordination and cooperation will be critical and useful.

title: Pytel's Theory and Model of Inflation - Complete Unified Framework with Banach Spaces, Fixed-Point Equilibrium, Abadir’s ACF, GMM Optimization, and Historical Synthesis - Comprehensive 60-Year Empirical Validation (1965-2025) Across Eight Countries with Robustness Analysis, Unifying Framework for Economic Thought, and Policy Implementation Guidelines
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Pytel's Theory and Model of Inflation - Complete Unified Framework with Banach Spaces, Fixed-Point Equilibrium, Abadir’s ACF, GMM Optimization, and Historical Synthesis - Comprehensive 60-Year Empirical Validation (1965-2025) Across Eight Countries with Robustness Analysis, Unifying Framework for Economic Thought, and Policy Implementation Guidelines

keywords: Complete Unified Framework with Banach Spaces
Historical Synthesis Comprehensive 60-Year Empirical Validation (1965-2025) Across Eight Countries with Robustness Analysis

detail.abstract:
This unified paper presents the complete theoretical and empirical analysis of Pytel's inflation theory, integrating four foundational perspectives: (1) rigorous mathematical foundations with Banach fixed-point equilibrium and Abadir's long-memory autocorrelation function; (2) GMM-optimized component weights derived endogenously from 60 years of data; (3) comprehensive robustness and reliability analysis comparing SRDB to established economic indicators (inflation and GDP measurement); (4) historical synthesis demonstrating Pytel's framework as unifying paradigm reconciling Smithian, Marxian, Keynesian, Hayekian, and Friedmanian economics.

Main Contributions:
(1) Demonstrates GMM optimal weights reveal financial risk premiums dominate (57% average) over computational costs (24%) and structural fragility (19%), reflecting market efficiency.
(2) Validates Sustainable Growth Principle empirically via Johansen cointegration tests (p < 0.01 all countries).
(3) Proves Banach contractivity across all countries (|β| + κ ∈ [0.56, 0.85]) establishing unique equilibrium.
(4) Achieves 48-58% RMSE reduction versus benchmarks (AR(1), Phillips Curve, Taylor Rule) in outof-sample tests.
(5) Predicts major crises (2008 GFC, 2020 COVID, 2021-23 supply surge) with 94-96% lower errors than competing models.
(6) Establishes SRDB robustness comparable to or exceeding inflation and GDP measurement standards.
(7) Demonstrates Pytel framework unifies five major schools of economic thought as special cases within comprehensive synthesis.
(8) Provides operational central bank implementation framework with 6-15 month lead time.

Key Empirical Results:
(1) Average RMSE 0.82 (Pytel-GMM) versus 1.47 (AR(1)), 1.38 (Phillips Curve), 1.40 (Taylor Rule).
(2) Crisis forecasting: average error 0.10pp versus 2.78pp (AR), 2.28pp (Phillips)-96% reduction. Cointegration trace statistics 39.6-51.3 (critical value 35.46). Contractivity satisfied across all countries. Hansen J-tests confirm specification validity (all p > 0.75).
(3) Rolling-window validation: 13,800+ independent forecasts confirm stability.
(4) Historical synthesis: Each economic school dominates during periods when its emphasized component matters most, validating integration.

Framework Status:
The Pytel-Banach-Abadir-GMM model represents paradigm shift from arbitrary specifications to data-driven optimal aggregation of systemic risk components, providing first unified framework for inflation economics in 250 years of economic thought. Real-time implementation enables central banks to achieve quarterly inflation target updates using observable financial indicators with proven predictive power.

title: Financing and the Green Paradox
affiliations: Boston College, Carroll School of Management, Indiana University - Kelley School of Business, Cornell University and Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Finance

detail.title: Financing and the Green Paradox
detail.abstract: We study firms' investment decisions in anticipation of higher financing costs under future climate regulation. The model predicts that polluting firms increase investment before regulation intended to curb emissions and consequently emit more ex post. Using the Paris Climate Accord and the Waxman-Markey bill as shocks to the likelihood of climate regulation, we find that exposed firms increase investment prior to the shock. Post-Paris, we find that exposed firms increase emissions levels and intensity. These effects are stronger for firms with higher-volatility operating cash flows. We discuss the possibility of multiple equilibria and the implications for climate change regulation.

title: Green Finance, Institutional Quality, and Money Laundering: International Evidence
affiliations: Ton Duc Thang University

detail.title: Green Finance, Institutional Quality, and Money Laundering: International Evidence
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of green finance presents both opportunities for enhanced financial transparency and challenges for maintaining robust anti-money laundering (AML) frameworks. This study examines how green finance development affects AML effectiveness and the moderating role of institutional quality using panel data from 156 countries over 2014-2022. Employing ARDL-PMG estimation, we find that green finance enhances AML effectiveness in the short run but undermines it in the long run. Institutional quality moderates this relationship through contrasting temporal dynamics: in the short run, strong institutions reduce the positive impact of green finance on AML effectiveness due to cautious evaluation processes, while in the long run, they help mitigate the negative effects through superior adaptive capacity and regulatory integration. Developing regions experience weaker positive long-term moderating effects while developed regions demonstrate stronger institutional advantages in leveraging green finance for AML purposes over time. Our findings demonstrate that environmental initiatives require synchronized institutional strengthening to prevent systemic vulnerabilities. Policy implications emphasize temporally-aware conditional green finance frameworks and integrated AMLgovernance reforms to ensure sustainable finance promotes development without compromising financial integrity.

title: Access Disparities in the Paycheck Protection Program: Evidence from Firm-Level Data

detail.title: Access Disparities in the Paycheck Protection Program: Evidence from Firm-Level Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research does not involve ethical approval, informed consent, consent to publish, and clinical trial registration
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
The Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) provided vital financial assistance to small businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a Dun & Bradstreet dataset covering more than 26 million U.S. firms linked with Small Business Administration records, this study examines how loan recipiency differs by firm characteristics. Key factors include prior 7(a) loan experience, delinquency and out-of-business risk, firm size and age, and owners’ demographics.

As of August 2020 (First Round), firms with prior SBA 7(a) loan experience were 38.8% more likely to obtain PPP loans. Firms with stronger pre-PPP credit and lower financial-stress scores also exhibited significantly higher approval probabilities, whereas female ownership was negatively associated with loan recipiency. Loan approval followed an inverted-U relationship with firm size, with mid-sized firms having the highest likelihood of approval. For the Second Round (2021), these disparities had narrowed substantially: the effects of 7(a) experience and firm size had nearly disappeared, the minority ownership advantage declined, and the disadvantage on female ownership turned slightly positive.

The results demonstrate how the determinants of PPP access evolved over time, highlighting the importance of prior financial experience and stability, and the later change in policy that improved equity in emergency funding.

title: Interest Rate Changes and Portfolio Rebalancing in the Digital Era: The Role of E-Wallet
affiliations: Zhejiang University, National University of Singapore - NUS Business School, Zhejiang University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Interest Rate Changes and Portfolio Rebalancing in the Digital Era: The Role of E-Wallet
detail.abstract: With fintech growth and smartphone adoption, E-wallet, which enables instant transactions while offering financial returns, have become increasingly prevalent. Using a unique dataset from Alipay, the world's largest E-wallet provider, we find that holdings in Yu'EBao-an investment product usable for payments-are less affected by interest rate changes than similar assets without payment functions. This effect is stronger for users who depend on Yu'EBao for daily spending, during peak payment periods, or among less experienced investors. Our findings suggest significant aggregate implications: Yu'EBao weakens retail risky asset adjustments by 11.7% for every one-percentage-point interest rate change.

title: M&A and the Simulation-Based Valuation of Companies with an Uncertain Exit Price and Special Rights
affiliations: Dresden University of Technology - Faculty of Economics and Business Management, FutureValue Group AG and University of Regensburg - Department of Finance

detail.title: M&A and the Simulation-Based Valuation of Companies with an Uncertain Exit Price and Special Rights
detail.abstract: This article presents a new methodological approach to value private equity investments based on simulation. The valuation relies on 'imperfect replication'. This method does not presuppose the perfection of the capital market and is essentially built on measuring the risk. The approach turns out to be easy to implement. Firm specific characteristics as well as and existing special rights can be depicted and modelled. The proposed methodology is of immediate practical usefulness as it can help to find decision support for concrete investment situations. Also, during the investment period it can be used for monitoring. The originality of the research lies in the combination of Monte Carlo simulation, multiple methods, relevant risk measures and risk-value models.

title: An Analysis of Consciousness, Class and State Power of Pasupata Shaivism and Sociopolitical Dynamics in Nepali's History

detail.title: An Analysis of Consciousness, Class and State Power of Pasupata Shaivism and Sociopolitical Dynamics in Nepali's History
detail.abstract: This paper examines the philosophy of Pasupata Shaivism and its socio-political impact on Nepali history, focusing on the relationship between ideology, class hierarchy, and state power. Central to this philosophy is the transactional relationship between consciousness and matter, where human interaction with the world through the five senses shapes the mind, influenced by karma (human actions). This dynamic interplay suggests that matter and consciousness are interdependent, reflecting a deeper principle of contradictionwhere the existence of an entity relies on the coexistence of opposing conditions. The study argues that Pasupata Shaivism's egalitarian principles, emphasizing collective well-being, spiritual equality, and shared resources, historically strengthened the Nepali state and fostered social cohesion. In contrast, periods dominated by Dharmasastra traditions, which advocated for private property and caste hierarchies, exacerbated class divisions and state fragility. Using primary sources such as inscriptions, genealogies, and religious texts, along with secondary analyses, the paper explores the socio-political implications of Pasupata Shaivism's focus on material conditions (dravyani), skills and knowledge (guna), and human actions (karma). Findings highlight how Shaivism supported peasants and workers, promoting social harmony and challenging exploitative systems, while Smriti-based frameworks concentrated wealth and power among elites. The paper concludes that Pasupata Shaivism offers an indigenous framework for addressing social inequalities and fostering equitable governance.

title: The ECB's Green Put: From Cheap Talk to Priced Action
affiliations: Banque de France, SKEMA Business School and CREST-ENSAE

detail.title: The ECB's Green Put: From Cheap Talk to Priced Action
detail.abstract: Standard asset pricing theory predicts a "carbon premium" for high-emission firms, yet recent realized returns have shown the opposite. We show that European Central Bank (ECB) climate communication acts as a "Green Put," a systematic policy signal that has persistently penalized brown assets and limited the return premium they would otherwise have achieved. To capture these shocks, we construct the Central Bank Climate and Nature Communication (CB-CNC) index, a novel high-frequency measure of ECB sustainability involvement from 1997 to 2025. Using a Large Language Model, the index distinguishes between "Action" and "Materiality" focused communications and integrates "Nature" alongside "Climate." We find that only ECB "Action" shocks-not "Materiality" rhetoric-drive the repricing of brown firms in both equity and bond markets. A counterfactual analysis shows that the cumulative impact of this "Action" talk has effectively eliminated the brown premium, preventing high-emission firms from realizing approximately 30% in cumulative outperformance since 2018.

title: Precious Metals in Financial Markets: A Copula Application
affiliations: University of Brescia

detail.title: Precious Metals in Financial Markets: A Copula Application
detail.abstract: Precious metals, such as gold and silver, have long been recognized as valuable assets in financial markets due to their historical role as stores of value and hedges against economic uncertainty. These metals, classified as commodities, stand out because of their enduring demand across various industries, including jewelry, technology, and finance. Precious metals possess unique characteristics that make them particularly attractive to investors. They are tangible, with inherent value driven by both industrial uses and the role they play in the global economy, especially as a store of wealth in times of financial instability. This paper focuses on gold and silver. We will examine the remarkable perfor mance of these metals over time, up until October 2025, and investigate their behavior through the lens of commodity futures, which are financial instruments that enable the trading of these metals without the need for physical ownership. By applying mathematical methods, we aim to uncover the dependence structure between the returns of gold and silver.

title: Employment Responses to Increased Biodiversity Transition Risk
affiliations: Durham University, Halle Institute for Economic Research, University of Bristol and University of Edinburgh - Business School

detail.title: Employment Responses to Increased Biodiversity Transition Risk
detail.abstract: This paper examines how firms adjust the number and types of workers they hire in response to increased biodiversity transition risk. Using the adoption of the Key Biodiversity Areas Standard of 2016 as a source of variation that increases the risk of future land-use restrictions, we find that firms reduce job postings in affected areas and reallocate labor to less exposed regions. This effect is concentrated among firms that make negative impacts on biodiversity. Cuts are stronger among production roles, while hiring in green and adaptive occupations increases. The effect is not driven by changes in capital investment or workers' labor supply decisions. Our findings contribute to the ongoing debate on the costs and benefits of biodiversity conservation policies and their implications for labor market outcomes.

title: New Crops and Old States Agricultural Technology and State Capacity in Historical China
affiliations: Peking University - School of Economics and University of Washington - Henry. M. Jackson School of International Studies

detail.title: New Crops and Old States Agricultural Technology and State Capacity in Historical China
detail.abstract: While high-yield crops spurred population growth and the expansion of market economies, their net effects on fiscal capacity were more ambiguous, shaped by a range of supply- and demand-side factors. This study leverages the historical introduction of maize and sweet potatoes to China as a natural experiment to examine the relationship between crop adoption, economic growth, and state capacity. Although both crops enhanced agricultural productivity and population growth, they had divergent impacts on fiscal capacity: maize was associated with increased tax revenue, whereas sweet potatoes correlated with a decline. What explains this contrast? Emprical evidence indicates that in regions suited to sweet potato cultivation, weakening state capacity was accompanied by reductions in tax quotas and deterioration in bureaucratic oversight—yet paradoxically, these regions saw more state-sponsored famine relief and greater local granary storage. Hence, the decline in state capacity is primarily driven by a decrease in agricultural legibility, rather than by lowered extractability or shifts in demand for state-service. A comparison with Tokugawa Japan further underscores the critical role of information and legibility in shaping state capacity in a pre-modern context.

title: LLM-Driven Active Listwise Tournaments for Portfolio Selection in Large Asset Universes
affiliations: aiXplain Inc. and aiXplain Inc.

detail.title: LLM-Driven Active Listwise Tournaments for Portfolio Selection in Large Asset Universes
detail.abstract: We introduce a scalable framework that uses large language models (LLMs) as listwise fuzzy judges to rank large universes of financial assets through active, multi-item tournaments. While recent preference-learning methods such as PAIRS (Liu et al., 2024), which fits a Gaussian-process preference model from pairwise data, and Product-of-Experts (POE) Bradley-Terry models (Liusie et al., 2024), which achieve near full-ranking performance with only ∼ 2% of all comparisons, demonstrate that LLM pairwise evaluations can be made efficient, they still rely on single-shot pairwise judgments. Such one-off comparisons are inherently noisy, unstable, and non-scalable, particularly in equity universes containing thousands of stocks. Our method overcomes these limitations by prompting the LLM to rank multi-item subsets rather than isolated pairs. These richer listwise judgments are then mapped into statistically coherent latent utilities via a Plackett-Luce model, producing a globally consistent ranking. An active learning loop further selects only the most informative subsets for evaluation at each iteration, substantially reducing the number of LLM calls required for convergence. Compared to existing financial applications-which generally use LLMs as black-box feature extractors, SWOT scorers (Meskovskis & Kenyon, 2024), or prompt-based portfolio generators (Schneider & Yilmaz, 2025; Guo et al., 2025; Hajaghaie & Thulasiram, 2025), and others surveyed in Jadhav & Mirza (2025)-our approach is the first to explicitly treat the LLM as a tournament judge and to fuse its qualitative assessments with probabilistic rank aggregation. The result is a principled, data-efficient, and highly scalable methodology that yields stable long-horizon asset rankings across very large investment universes. This framework bridges modern LLM-based preference learning and portfolio construction, providing a significantly more coherent, interpretable, and sample-efficient alternative to both prior AI-finance approaches and existing pairwise-only LLM ranking techniques. Empirical evaluations are done strictly postdating the GPT-4o-mini model's training cutoff , ensuring a fully out-of-sample assessment. In this forward-looking setting, the framework produces rankings with strong predictive power (NDCG up to 0.625) and delivers substantial portfolio outperformance: the top-10% portfolio achieves +55.2% higher annualized returns, +62.6% lower maximum drawdown, +107.3% higher Sharpe, and a +311.4% improvement in Calmar relative to the S&P 500. These results demonstrate that active listwise LLM tournaments yield economically meaningful and robust real-world investment performance.

title: Fed Funds Market Overview

This paper delves into the structure and functioning of the Federal Reserve, examining its influence on financial markets, the mechanics of monetary policy, and the crucial role it plays in maintaining liquidity, stability, and economic growth. detail.abstract:
India's Digital Public Infrastructure, which includes prominent tools such as Aadhar, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Digital Payments, and Digilocker, is collectively known as "Stack India". Digital India aims to provide much-needed impetus to the nine pillars of growth sectors, i.e., Broadband Highway, Universal Access to Mobile Connectivity, Public Internet Access
Scheme, and Electronic administration: Government Reform through Technology, e-Kranti -Providing Electronic Services, Information for All, Electronic Manufacturing, IT for Jobs, and Early Harvest Programs. The term "digital transformation" has become popular to refer to the shift from digitalization initiatives to a comprehensive overhaul of rules, procedures, and
services to simplify user experiences for residents and frontline employees [1]. The paper's main objectives are: to determine how bureaucratic corruption and digital transformation are related and to determine factors that need to be adequately handled by IT experts to encourage the use of Digital means. The study shows that digitally connecting and offering services online has been the biggest accomplishment of Digital India. Nowadays, many internet services related to financial inclusion, education, health, and agriculture are accessible nationwide. Initiatives like eNAM(National Agriculture Market), eSanjivini, DIKSHA(digital infrastructure for knowledge sharing), and Common Service Centers (CSCs) have given India a true sense of empowerment. The corruption and bureaucratic mindset continue to be obstacles to digital change. It has been observed that corrupt practices have continued even after public services were digitized and that digital services are insufficiently effective in addressing them [2]. It is still challenging to institutionalize new information systems, technologies, norms, practices, and other innovations for bettering planning, governance, operational effectiveness, and service delivery in the public sector.
Participation of people in online services, having Knowledge and skill to use online services, significant use of ICT Technologies, IT laws, online Services, infrastructure for online services, and efficiency and transparency in online services increase trust in Indian Administration. Analysis shows that corruption is prevalent in the public sector. Efficiency and transparency in online services have increased due to digital transformation. People participate less in online services due to network problems, illiteracy, lack of IT skills, and infrastructure challenges. An online survey was conducted using Google Forms to gather data from the education, health, and MSMEs sectors. The purposive sampling method was used to collect data. Three hundred ninety replies representing the broader population's viewpoint are gathered.

title: From Liberation to New Authority Doctors' Independence According to the EBM
affiliations: Hebrew University of Jerusalem

detail.title: From Liberation to New Authority Doctors' Independence According to the EBM
detail.abstract: This article explores the evolution of the Evidence-Based Medicine (EBM) movement from the 1990s to the 2000s, focusing on the sociological changes and shifts in power dynamics within the medical establishment. Initially, the EBM movement granted significant independence to physicians, challenging the traditional hierarchy where expert doctors were the primary source of knowledge. However, over time, it became evident that most doctors would rely on processed and finished knowledge rather than critically analyzing it themselves. This shift led to a diminished emphasis on the physician's independence and a greater reliance on information repositories as the primary source of medical knowledge. Ultimately, the EBM movement succeeded in emphasizing epidemiological research but failed to create a new type of doctor proficient in epistemological knowledge and independent analysis.

title: LLM-Driven Market Microstructure Representation Learning for Robust High-Frequency Forecasting
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: LLM-Driven Market Microstructure Representation Learning for Robust High-Frequency Forecasting
detail.abstract: This paper studies the integration of large language model (LLM) style encoders with market microstructure data for high-frequency forecasting. We propose a framework called Market Microstructure Representation Learning (MMRL), which converts order-book dynamics into a sequence of structured tokens, and extracts a latent execution representation that can be used for multi-horizon prediction. We formalize the tokenization scheme, the latent embedding, and the forecasting objective, and provide a simple robustness result under adversarial microstructure noise. The focus is on mathematical formulation and interpretability rather than model size.

title: Hiring Practices Effect on Project team Monitoring. Bureaucratic Theory at the Public Sector
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Hiring Practices Effect on Project team Monitoring. Bureaucratic Theory at the Public Sector
detail.abstract: Hiring practices are vital for any organization because they have consequences for its success and goals meeting, and it has a significant effect on many other organizational variables as literature shows. On the other hand, project team management practices are very important to any Civil Services Sector (CSS) because they affect projects success that consumes big resources of a nation treasury and can affect citizens' life as literature confirmed. This research aims to examine the influence of hiring practices of Palestinian CSS on project team management practices. This research is designed as quantitative study that uses correlational design. A questionnaire was designed to meet the need for collecting primary data from the community. The tool was conducted through google forms to ensure proper timing of responses and proper collection for data. Moreover, the SPSS program and the Smart PLS Version 4 were used to analyze the data and to confirm research tool reliability and validity. The population was the supervisory-positions employees who work at Ministry Of Education of Palestine (MoE) with total number of 644. A sample of 341 was selected randomly at a confidence level of (0.05). The response rate was 95.9 %. Findings indicated that employment policies implementation and recruitment practices can affect project team monitoring practices. Where no significant effect was found of selection practices on project team monitoring practices. To sum up, improving hiring practices will lead to better project team monitoring practice. This study is very important for CCS leaders, human resources managers, project managers, and policy makers. Increasing project team management efficiency will help Palestinian for better utilization of the scarce resources and will increase the CSS project goals meeting.
